advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Widen the verb-token regex (or assert the charset) so a future confirmable route name with a digit/uppercase isn't silently truncated into a spurious prose-drift report.
evidence: _CONFIRM_SCOPE is derived from live route names (src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:680: `derived["_CONFIRM_SCOPE"] = frozenset(r.name for r in live if r.confirmable)`); nothing constrains a future route name to `[a-z][a-z-]*`.
ABSENCE: no comment or assertion documents the assumed verb-name charset, so a future verb like `set-file-2impact` would be silently mis-parsed rather than flagged.
advisory.finding: The verb-name capture regex `` `([a-z][a-z-]*)` `` only matches lowercase-and-hyphen tokens. If a future confirmable route name contains a digit or uppercase letter, the gate would silently truncate or drop that verb from the parsed prose set, producing a spurious drift report (blaming the prose) rather than a clear signal — and the truncation is invisible. Not a present bug (all current confirmable names conform) but a latent maintainability trap given the gate exists precisely to catch future verb additions.
